original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Unless otherwise indicated, all commercial reagents and anhydrous solvents were used without additional purification. 1H NMR spectra were recorded with a Bruker BioSpin GmbH 400 spectrometer. Chemical shifts (in ppm) were referenced to tetramethylsilane (δ = 0 ppm) in DMSO, or CHCl3 as an internal standard (2.5, 3.31/4.87, 7.26 ppm). 13C NMR spectra were obtained by the same NMR spectrometer and were calibrated with DMSO (δ = 39.51, 49.1, 77.2 ppm). HRMS was recorded on a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Q Exactive mass spectrometer. Thin-layer chromatograms were performed on EMD TLC silica gel 60 F254 aluminum-backed plates and visualized with UV light. Reactions were monitored by walkup Shimadzu LCMS/UV system with LC-30AD solvent pump, 2020 MS, Sil-30AC autosampler, SPD-M30A UV detector, CTO-20A column oven, using 2–98% CH3CN/0.1% formic acid (or 0.01% ammonia) over 2.5 min (short method) or 5.5 min (long method) OR Waters Acquity LCMS system using 2–98% CH3CN/0.1% formic acid (or 0.1% ammonia) over 2 min (short method) or 5 min (long method). Flash column chromatography purifications were done on a Teledyne Isco Combiflash Rf utilizing Silicycle HP columns. Reverse-phase purification was carried out on a Phenomenex Gemini-NX C18 (30 mm × 100 mm, 5 μm) with a gradient of 5–95% CH3CN/H2O (with 0.1% formic acid or 0.1% NH4OH) over 10 min at 60 mL/min. Analytical purity was greater than 95% unless stated otherwise. Purity determinations were performed on an Agilent 1200 HPLC coupled with Agilent MSD mass spectrometer using ESI as ionization source. The LC separation used a Phenomenex XB-C18, 1.7 mm, 50 mm × 2.1 mm column with a 0.4 mL/min flow rate. Solvent A was H2O with 0.1% FA, and solvent B was CH3CN with 0.1% FA. The gradient consisted of 2–98% solvent B over 7 min and hold 98% B for 1.5 min following equilibration for 1.5 min. LC column temperature was 40 °C. UV was collected at 220 and 254 nm. Mass spectrometry full scan was applied to all LC experiments. See below for experimental steps for synthesis of all final analogues in the above text. Some general procedures (A–F) are provided at the end of the Experimental Section. Experiments for the synthesis and analysis of key intermediates are presented in the Supporting Information.
